responsibility: This module is GCC’s target backend for the eBPF architecture, covering the target description, option handling, code generation hooks, and BPF-specific metadata emission needed to compile C-family code into Linux kernel/loadable BPF objects. Its core files define the static ABI and machine model (registers, data layout, calling conventions, assembler syntax, and target options), the RTL instruction-selection patterns, constraints, predicates, and atomic operations that map GCC middle-end operations onto BPF instructions and ISA-version features, and the imperative target hooks that implement prologues/epilogues, calls, operand printing, builtins, attributes, and preprocessor macros. A major distinguishing responsibility of this module is BPF ecosystem integration: it models kernel helper functions and helper-call attributes, exposes packet-load and CO-RE builtins, runs BPF-specific passes for preserve_access_index handling, and constructs/emits .BTF.ext CO-RE, function, and line metadata so generated objects can interoperate with kernel helpers and loader-side BTF-based relocation mechanisms.
